samples.summary: The image cut path (Cmd/Ctrl+X on a click-selected image) has no test at all, despite being the only document-mutating branch added by this diff
samples.evidence: The diff adds a `cut` branch in `TextEditor.handleCut` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1224-1232) that writes the image to the clipboard and then invokes `imageDeleteHandler` → `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2243-2255), and adds `key === 'x'` absorption in `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:~2300). The new suite only ever dispatches `copy` (`dispatchCopy`, line 74) and only ever presses `'c'`/`'C'` (`pressCopyShortcut`, line 87). Grep for `handleCut|imageDeleteHandler|dispatchCut|'x'` across packages/docs/test returns nothing. If the removal, the clipboard write ordering, the undo snapshot, or the `x` key routing is wrong, a user loses an image with nothing on the clipboard and no test fails.

samples.summary: Test named 'an image selection is ignored when there is also a text selection' never selects an image, so it is vacuous coverage for the precedence it claims to test
samples.evidence: The test body (lines 279-291) calls only `editor._setSelectionForTest(...)`; it never calls `editor.selectImageAt('b1', 2)`, so no image selection exists. The assertions (`text/plain === 'ab'`, `blocks[0].inlines[0].style.image` undefined) hold identically for a plain text copy with no image selection at all — i.e. they pass whether or not `handleCopy`'s text-selection-first precedence is correct. If the precedence were inverted (image branch preferred), this test would still pass while user copies of text over a selected image would silently write the image instead.

samples.summary: The nested-table branch of the new `getSelectedBlocks` cell resolution is untested — every table test uses a top-level table
samples.evidence: The diff resolves the cell via `resolveNestedTableLayout(cellInfo.tableBlockId, layout)` with the comment '(not `layout.blocks.find`) so a cell inside a nested table resolves too'. All three #872 tests (copy-integrity.test.ts:147, 166, 180) build a single top-level `createTableBlock(1,1)`, which would also pass with a plain `layout.blocks.find`. Nothing exercises a table nested inside a cell, so a regression there would again silently drop styles/images from the clipboard.

Every image test in copy-integrity.test.ts reads only `written.get(WAFFLEDOCS_MIME)` via `payloadBlocks`; `text/plain` is asserted only on the text/table paths (lines 162, 287). An external paste target receiving the wrong plain-text flavour would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The modifier guards in the new image copy/cut key routing (`!e.shiftKey && !e.altKey`, and the Mac/non-Mac `metaKey` vs `ctrlKey` branch) are untested
samples.evidence: `pressCopyShortcut` (copy-integrity.test.ts:87) always sets BOTH `metaKey` and `ctrlKey` and never `shiftKey`/`altKey` — deliberately 'OS-agnostic', which means neither branch of the `navigator.platform` test is discriminated, and no test asserts that e.g. Cmd+Shift+C still falls through to the catch-all that clears the image selection. A broken guard would swallow unrelated shortcuts with no failing test.

samples.summary: The defensive null paths in `imageSelectionProvider` (block deleted by a peer → `findBlock` null; no image at offset) have no test
samples.evidence: The provider's comment justifies using `findBlock` over `getBlock` because a remote peer's deletion would otherwise throw out of the browser `copy` listener and wipe the system clipboard — a stated user-visible risk. No test in copy-integrity.test.ts (or elsewhere; grep `imageSelectionProvider` across packages/docs matches only src) selects an image and then removes the block/image before dispatching copy.

samples.summary: The extracted `deleteSelectedImageInline` (Delete/Backspace on a selected image, including its `readOnly` early-return) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff moves the Delete/Backspace deletion body into `deleteSelectedImageInline` and adds a `if (readOnly || !selectedImage) return;` guard that did not exist at the old call site. Grep for `selectImageAt` across packages/docs/test matches only copy-integrity.test.ts, which never dispatches Delete/Backspace; grep for `imageKeyHandler`/`clearImageSelection` in packages/docs/test finds no delete coverage. The behaviour is pre-existing but the refactor plus new guard ships unverified.

verdict.reason: The image-cut branch is real and genuinely untested. text-editor.ts:1224-1232 adds a no-text-selection cut path that writes the image to the clipboard and then calls imageDeleteHandler -> deleteSelectedImageInline (editor.ts:2242-2252, wired at 2268), which snapshots and deletes the inline; editor.ts:2298 absorbs mod+'x' in imageKeyHandler. No test anywhere exercises it: copy-integrity.test.ts only builds `new Event('copy')` (line 80) and only presses 'c'/'C' (lines 87, 216, 229, 240, 254); the only real cut dispatches in the package are editor-read-only.test.ts:155-176, both with a text selection set via _setSelectionForTest, so handleCut takes the selection branch (or the readOnly early return at text-editor.ts:1219) and never reaches the image branch. Repo-wide greps for imageDeleteHandler/deleteSelectedImageInline, selectImageAt/getSelectedImage, and key 'x'/KeyX turn up no test; frontend docs-context-menu.test.tsx only mocks a `cut` callback and asserts menu-item visibility. A defect in the removal, clipboard ordering, undo snapshot, or 'x' routing would silently destroy an image with an empty clipboard and no test would fail — a data-affecting gap, hence major.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: the test 'an image selection is ignored when there is also a text selection' (copy-integrity.test.ts:279-291) calls only `_setSelectionForTest` and never `selectImageAt`, so no image selection exists (`getSelectedImage` returns null when `selectedImage` is unset, editor.ts:3652-3663). `handleCopy` (text-editor.ts:1188-1198) consults the image provider only inside `if (!this.selection.hasSelection())`; with a text selection and no image selection, the assertions (`text/plain === 'ab'`, no image inline) are produced by the ordinary text path (1210-1213) and would hold identically under an inverted precedence. The scenario is reachable and testable — `_setSelectionForTest` (editor.ts:3790-3796) does not clear `selectedImage`, so `selectImageAt('b1',2)` + `_setSelectionForTest(...)` would exercise the real precedence. This is fake coverage for the named behavior on the clipboard write path, squarely in the test-adequacy lane; no guard makes it moot and no ground for refutation applies.
